newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Leumi completes Africa Israel sale.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi completes Africa Israel sale.

text.p: Bank Leumi said on Wednesday it had completed the sale of a controlling stake in Africa Israel Investments Ltd to Israeli businessman Lev Leviev for $190 million.
Leviev paid $141 million for Leumi's Africa Israel holding and another $49 million for shares controlled by Israeli businessmen Mordechai Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer in package deal, Leumi said.
The combined stakes are equal to 46.58 percent of equity and 54.2 percent of voting rights in Africa Israel, a property development company with interests in tourism and building projects.
The purchase price was based on a company valuation of $400 million.
As a result of the agreement signed late on Tuesday, Leumi's stake in Africa Israel will drop to 25 percent to comply with Israeli banking reforms that require banks to reduce their non-bank assets.

Leviev also took a series of options to increase his holdings in Africa Israel over a two-year period enabling Leumi to reduce its Africa holding further to 20 percent by 1999 in line with the reforms.
The tender for Africa Israel was for the company shorn of its key insurance business, which is being spun off and sold to Italian insurer Generali SpA.
